blocks.text: The typhoon with the international name ‘Choi-wan’ has intensified into a Super Typhoon as of 8 p.m. Sunday, October 4. Choi-wan is currently still outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR) but is closely being monitored by weather bureau Pagasa. Choi-wan, based on a bulletin released Sunday night by Pagasa, is packing winds of 185 kilometer per hour (km/h) and gusts of 230 km/h. READ: Typhoon Choi-wan trough to bring rains, thunderstorms over VisMin Its location as of 8 p.m. is 2,600 kilometers east of extreme northern Luzon.
